items.note: Use 白 before a verb phrase when someone receives a benefit for free or without deserving the effort. Whether it works depends on the verb. Learners often assume 白 can modify any verb, but some combinations are unnatural.
Use 自从 to introduce a starting event, or put 以来 after a starting-time phrase, then state the continuing situation. Learners often misplace 以来 or put 很 after the adjective instead of before it.

早已 goes before a predicate to say that something was already true well before a reference time. Keep the subject before 早已; learners sometimes put the adverb after the predicate or before the subject.

items.en: They broke up long ago.
items.wrongPy: tā men fēn shǒu zǎo yǐ
items.why: 早已 must come before 分手; say “他们早已分手.”

items.note: 果然 goes before the predicate to show that an outcome confirms what was expected. Use it for an expected event or state, not just a guess. Learners often put it after the verb or place 了 between 果然 and the verb.

立刻 comes before a verb phrase to say that an action happens immediately after a relevant trigger. Learners often place it after the verb or between a verb and its object; keep it before the whole action.

items.en: He corrects it immediately.
items.wrongPy: tā gǎi zhèng lì kè
items.why: 立刻 must precede the verb phrase; say “他立刻改正.”

items.note: 似乎 and 仿佛 introduce a proposition that describes an impression or appearance, rather than a confirmed fact. They generally come before that proposition. Learners often put 很 before 似乎 or insert 似乎 inside the proposition.

In this 把 pattern, the object comes before a suitable verb, and the nominal result or label follows that verb. Use it to describe a changed relation, such as treating something as a category. Learners often put the label before the verb.

据 introduces a source, followed by a comma and the clause reporting its information; this relatively formal pattern attributes a claim. Learners sometimes reverse the source and 据 or break the source phrase apart, leaving 据 without a proper source.

通常 is a sentence adverb placed before the predicate to describe what is generally true while allowing exceptions. It can come first or immediately before a verb or adjective phrase. Learners often put it after the verb or inside the predicate.

假如 introduces a hypothetical condition, and 就 commonly introduces the resulting action or outcome. Use the pair to connect the two clauses; 就 can sometimes be omitted. Learners often place 就 inside the condition instead of before the consequence.

即将 is a relatively formal adverb meaning an event is impending. Put it before the verb phrase, after the subject; it does not itself mean the event has already happened. Learners often place it after the verb or between a verb and its object.

一旦 introduces a consequential condition, and 就 normally comes before the resulting action or state. Learners often move 就 into the condition or place it after the consequence instead of marking the result clause.

极其 is a relatively formal degree adverb placed before a gradable predicate to mean extremely. Learners may put it after the predicate, but Chinese degree adverbs in this pattern precede the quality or state they modify.

不但不/没有 + predicate，反而 + predicate marks an outcome that reverses what was expected. Use it to contrast an expected action with what actually happens; learners often put 不 after the verb instead of before it.
从而 introduces a result caused by the preceding clause. Use it to link an action or change to its consequence; learners often split 从而 or put it inside the first clause instead of before the result.

items.phrase: 回收家电从而防止破坏土地
items.zh: 回收家电，从而防止破坏土地。
items.en: Recycle appliances, thereby preventing damage to the land.
items.wrong: 回收家电，从而破坏防止土地。
items.wrongPy: huí shōu jiā diàn cóng ér pò huài fáng zhǐ tǔ dì
items.why: 防止 must precede the action it prevents; the correct result clause is 防止破坏土地.

items.note: Put 似的 immediately after the noun phrase to mean “like a snake”; the full expression then modifies the following noun. Learners may add another 的 or put 的 before 似的, breaking the fixed expression.
Use 从 + source + 来看 before the complete clause to limit the judgment to that evidence or perspective. Learners may place the source after 来看, but 从来看 does not introduce the source in this pattern.

items.phrase: 从数据来看结论很明确
items.zh: 从数据来看，结论很明确。
items.en: Judging from the data, the conclusion is clear.
items.wrong: 从来看数据，结论很明确。
items.wrongPy: cóng lái kàn shù jù jié lùn hěn míng què
items.why: The source must follow 从 and precede 来看; say 从数据来看.

items.note: 时常 goes before a verb phrase to describe an action that happens repeatedly. It does not mean an action continues without stopping. Learners may add 不 and accidentally change an affirmative statement about frequent action into one about frequent non-action.

items.en: She often enjoys Chinese paintings.
items.wrongPy: tā shí cháng bù xīn shǎng guó huà
items.why: 不 reverses the affirmative meaning; the phrase says she often enjoys Chinese paintings.

items.en: She often appreciates calligraphy.
items.wrongPy: tā shí cháng bù xīn shǎng shū fǎ
items.why: 不 reverses the affirmative meaning; the phrase says she often appreciates calligraphy.

items.note: Use 如此 immediately before a predicate to express a contextually supplied degree or manner. Learners may wrongly move the predicate before its subject. 如此 can also stand alone when context supplies the predicate, as in the fate phrase.

彼此 marks reciprocal participants: it can come before a predicate or after a verb as its object. Learners may place it before the subject, where it no longer has a grammatical role; do not confuse this pattern with adverbial 互相.

Use 要不然 or 不然 after a requirement to introduce what will happen if it is not met; 要不就 can also serve this function. Learners may mistakenly put the alternative marker inside the requirement instead of before the consequence.

items.phrase: 挑选图书要不然就没有了
items.zh: 挑选图书，要不然就没有了。
items.en: Choose the books, otherwise there won't be any.
items.wrong: 挑选图书，要不然就没有就了。
items.wrongPy: tiāo xuǎn tú shū yào bù rán jiù méi yǒu jiù le
items.why: 就 cannot be repeated this way; the consequence is 就没有了.

items.note: Put a number directly before 周 to express a duration in weeks; no measure word intervenes. Learners may insert 个 or reverse the number and 周. For example, say 两周, not 两个周.

items.en: He lived in the dorm for three weeks.
items.wrongPy: tā zài sù shè jū zhù le zhōu sān
items.why: The number must come before 周; the correct order is 他在宿舍居住了三周。

items.note: 毕竟 is a sentence adverb placed before the proposition it frames as decisive background. Use it when acknowledging other considerations but emphasizing this fact. Learners often put it after the proposition; it should come before the whole statement.

始终 comes before a predicate to say that a state or action continues from beginning to end. It can modify a positive or negative predicate. Learners may place it after the predicate, but it belongs before the predicate it modifies.

The measure word after a number depends on the noun: 颗 counts small rounded items, 支 counts slender items, and 根 counts long rods or stalks. Learners often choose by shape alone or overgeneralize one measure word; use the conventional pairing for each noun.

items.en: I have an orange.
items.wrongPy: wǒ yǒu yì zhī jú zi
items.why: 支 is not the conventional measure for an orange; say 我有一颗橘子。

items.en: A fruit is growing.
items.wrongPy: yì gēn guǒ shí zài shēng zhǎng
items.why: 根 does not count 果实 here; the phrase uses 颗, as in 一颗果实在生长。

items.note: 哪怕 introduces a condition, and 也 introduces the consequence that remains true even in that case. Use the paired pattern to emphasize that the result does not change. Learners often omit or move 也; it belongs at the start of the consequence.

过于 comes before a gradable description to say that something exceeds an appropriate degree. Place the subject before 过于 and the description after it. Learners may mistakenly put 过于 after the description, reversing the expected order.

items.en: The footsteps are too slow.
items.wrongPy: huǎn màn guò yú jiǎo bù
items.why: 过于 belongs before 缓慢 and after its subject; write “脚步过于缓慢。”

items.note: 便 introduces what follows as an ensuing result or immediate continuation, often in written style. Put it at the start of the second clause. Learners may place 便 inside that clause rather than before it.

格外 comes before a gradable predicate to indicate an exceptional degree compared with the usual situation. Learners may place it after the adjective as if it were a degree word that follows the predicate; here it must precede the predicate.

Put 反正 before the whole statement to signal that the conclusion holds despite disputed circumstances. It can also introduce an imperative-like proposal. Learners often move it inside the statement or treat it as a replacement for the proposition; the proposition still needs its own normal word order.

items.en: Anyway, he is safe.
items.wrongPy: píng ān fǎn zhèng tā
items.why: 反正 must introduce the proposition; the correct order is 反正他平安。

items.en: Anyway, the person concerned is present.
items.wrongPy: fǎn zhèng zài chǎng běn rén
items.why: The proposition needs normal subject-predicate order; the correct phrase is 反正本人在场。

items.en: Anyway, keep things as they are.
items.wrongPy: bǎo liú fǎn zhèng xiàn zhuàng
items.why: 反正 must not split the verb from its object; the correct phrase is 反正保留现状。

items.en: Anyway, he is at peace now.
items.wrongPy: fǎn zhèng tā le xīn ān
items.why: 了 belongs after 心安 here, not between 他 and 心安; the correct phrase is 反正他心安了。

items.note: 用不着 + a verb phrase says an action is unnecessary, not that someone is generally unable to do it. Learners sometimes put a particle between 用不着 and the verb phrase; keep the phrase together.

items.en: There is no need to come.
items.wrongPy: yòng bu zháo le qián lái
items.why: 了 cannot split 用不着 from its verb phrase; the correct phrase is 用不着前来。

items.en: There is no need to comfort him.
items.wrongPy: yòng bu zháo le ān wèi tā
items.why: 了 cannot split 用不着 from its verb phrase; the correct phrase is 用不着安慰他。

items.note: 同 and 以及 can join two noun phrases, while 都 can refer to the coordinated pair as a whole. Put 都 after both noun phrases and before the predicate. Learners sometimes place 都 inside the coordination, splitting the two nouns.

items.en: The back and waist are both sensitive.
items.wrongPy: bēi yǐ jí dōu yāo hěn mǐn gǎn
items.why: 都 cannot split 背 and 腰; write “背以及腰都很敏感。”

items.phrase: 报道以及宣传都在展开
items.zh: 报道以及宣传都在展开。
items.en: News reporting and publicity are underway.
items.wrong: 报道以及都宣传都在展开。
items.wrongPy: bào dào yǐ jí dōu xuān chuán dōu zài zhǎn kāi
items.why: The first 都 wrongly splits the nouns; write “报道以及宣传都在展开。”

items.note: Use a number followed by a measure word before the noun. 朵 counts individual blooms or cloud-like forms, while 束 counts gathered bunches or beams; the noun determines the suitable choice. Learners may use a measure word that does not fit the noun.

因而 links a cause to its consequence and gives the connection a relatively formal, written tone. Put the cause first and 因而 before the result. Learners may treat 因而 as a free-floating word; it belongs at the start of the result clause.

items.en: Refresh your skills and thereby improve.
items.wrongPy: chōng diàn yīn ér ér jìn bù
items.why: The repeated 而 is incorrect; use 因而 once, as in “充电，因而进步。”

items.note: 曾经 comes before a verb phrase to describe an experience or state that was true in the past, without saying whether it continues now. Learners may place it after the verb; keep it before the whole verb phrase.

得 introduces a complement that describes the degree or resulting state of an action or condition. Learners often put the description before 得; place 得 immediately before the complement, whose internal word order must remain intact.

items.en: The businesses are hyping it heavily.
items.wrongPy: shāng jiā chǎo de rè hěn
items.why: 很 must precede 热 in the complement; the correct order is 商家炒得很热。

items.en: I’m so cold I can’t move.
items.wrongPy: wǒ dòng de bù le dòng
items.why: 不了 cannot precede 动 in this complement; the correct order is 我冻得动不了。

items.note: 不得了 follows a subject or an adjective with 得 to express an extraordinary degree or a serious situation. It is an evaluative expression, not a way to say someone cannot finish something. Learners may put it before the subject or omit the required 得 after an adjective.

items.en: The rainstorm is terrible.
items.wrongPy: bù dé liǎo bào yǔ
items.why: 不得了 follows the subject; the correct phrase is 暴雨不得了。

items.en: The situation is extremely serious.
items.wrongPy: bù dé liǎo xíng shì
items.why: 不得了 follows the subject; the correct phrase is 形势不得了。

items.en: This package is something else.
items.wrongPy: bāo guǒ bù dé liǎo zhè
items.why: 这包裹 must precede its evaluation; the correct phrase is 这包裹不得了。

items.en: I’m terribly cold.
items.wrongPy: wǒ dòng bù dé liǎo de
items.why: 得 must precede 不得了 after 冻; the correct phrase is 我冻得不得了。

items.en: This stimulus is extraordinary.
items.wrongPy: cì jī bù dé liǎo zhè ge
items.why: 这个刺激 must precede its evaluation; the correct phrase is 这个刺激不得了。

items.en: Literary achievements are extraordinary.
items.wrongPy: bù dé liǎo wén xué chéng jiù
items.why: 不得了 follows the subject; the correct phrase is 文学成就不得了。

items.note: 的确 comes before a predicate to affirm that a claim really holds. It can modify a verb or an adjective phrase. Learners may move it into the predicate; keep 的确 before the complete predicate.
朝 goes before a place to show the direction of movement or orientation, followed by the verb phrase when there is one. Learners may put the verb before the place; keep the place directly after 朝.

items.en: Walk eastward.
items.wrongPy: cháo zǒu dōng fāng
items.why: The place 东方 must follow 朝 and come before 走; the correct order is 朝东方走。

items.note: Use 反而 between two clauses when the second result reverses what the first circumstance leads you to expect. Keep the first clause before 反而. Learners may wrongly move 反而 to the start or mistake it for a general-purpose word meaning “but.”

items.en: He started a business, but it failed.
items.wrongPy: chuàng yè tā fǎn ér dào le
items.why: The subject must come before 创业 here; the correct order is 他创业，反而倒了。

items.note: Use 群 for groups of people or animals, 批 for batches, and 副 for matched sets. The measure word must fit the noun; learners often choose one just because it means a group or set in English.

Put 刚好 before the predicate to say that a circumstance or amount happens to fit exactly. Learners may insert a particle inside a fixed predicate, such as 在场, or move 刚好 into a position that breaks the phrase.

items.en: I happen to be there.
items.wrongPy: wǒ gāng hǎo zài le chǎng
items.why: 在场 is a fixed predicate, so 了 cannot split it; the correct phrase is 我刚好在场。

items.en: He happened to be there.
items.wrongPy: tā gāng hǎo zài le chǎng
items.why: 在场 is a fixed predicate, so 了 cannot split it; the correct phrase is 他刚好在场。

items.note: In this colloquial emphatic passive, place the agent after 被、叫、or 让, then put 给 before the bounded verb phrase. Learners often put 给 after the verb, where it no longer marks this passive construction.

items.phrase: 方案被这个人给否定了
items.zh: 方案被这个人给否定了
items.en: The plan was rejected by this person.
items.wrong: 方案被这个人否定给了
items.wrongPy: fāng àn bèi zhè ge rén fǒu dìng gěi le
items.why: For this passive, 给 must come before 否定, not after it; the correct order is 方案被这个人给否定了。

items.note: 根本 goes before a negative predicate to reject a claim completely, as in 根本不搞 or 根本不合法. Learners often put 根本 after 不; keep the adverb before the negation.

items.en: They don’t do engineering at all.
items.wrongPy: bù gēn běn gǎo gōng chéng
items.why: 根本 must precede 不 in this pattern; the correct order is 根本不搞工程。

items.note: 过来 and 过去 follow a verb to express a direction or, with certain verbs, a change of state. Learners can misplace 了, which follows the verb and precedes the directional complement in these examples.

items.en: He came over.
items.wrongPy: tā le guò lái
items.why: 了 cannot go before the verb; the correct order is 他过来了。

items.en: He went over (there).
items.wrongPy: tā le guò qù
items.why: 了 cannot go before the verb; the correct order is 他过去了。

items.en: He didn't go over.
items.wrongPy: tā guò méi yǒu qù
items.why: 没有 must precede the directional complement; the correct order is 他没有过去。

items.en: They came over too.
items.wrongPy: tā men guò lái yě le
items.why: 也 cannot separate 过来 from 了 here; the correct order is 她们也过来了。

items.note: 行 is the measure word for rows or lines and goes between the number and the noun. Use it when counting rows, not levels. Learners often omit this measure word and put the noun directly after 两.

items.en: There are two rows of headings.
items.wrongPy: yǒu liǎng biāo tí
items.why: A number needs the row measure word 行 here; the correct phrase is 有两行标题。

items.note: Use 或是 before each of two alternative possibilities. This presents alternatives rather than asking a question. Learners may put 或是 after an option or omit it before the second option; keep one marker at the start of each option.

items.en: Either black or gray.
items.wrongPy: hēi huò shì huò shì huī sè
items.why: 或是 must introduce each option; the correct order is 或是黑，或是灰色。

items.note: A number and 册 or 集 come before the noun they count: 册 counts bound volumes, while 集 counts installments or episodes. Choose the unit that fits the publication. Learners may put the unit after the noun or place 的 between the demonstrative and unit.

items.en: This classic book is very old.
items.wrongPy: zhè jīng diǎn cè hěn gǔ lǎo
items.why: 册 must precede 经典; the correct phrase is 这册经典很古老。

items.en: The myth in this episode is mysterious.
items.wrongPy: zhè de jí shén huà hěn shén mì
items.why: 的 cannot go between 这 and 集; the correct phrase is 这集的神话很神秘。

items.note: 凭 + basis + verb phrase means doing something by relying on a resource, credential, or evidence. Put the basis after 凭 and before the action; learners often move the object ahead of its verb or attach 的 incorrectly.

items.en: Judge him by his character.
items.wrongPy: pǐn zhì píng píng jià tā
items.why: 凭 introduces the basis before the action; the correct order is 凭品质评价他.

items.en: Judge his character based on the evaluation.
items.wrongPy: píng píng jià tā de pǐn zhì kàn
items.why: 他的品质 is the object of 看 and must follow it; the correct order is 看他的品质.

items.note: 亲自 comes after the subject and before the verb phrase to show that someone does something personally, rather than delegating it. Learners may put it before the subject or after the verb; keep it immediately before the action phrase.

items.en: He takes the photos himself.
items.wrongPy: qīn zì tā shè yǐng
items.why: 亲自 must follow the subject and precede the action; put it after 他.

items.en: I’ll sign it myself.
items.wrongPy: qīn zì wǒ qiān zì
items.why: The subject 我 must come before 亲自, which precedes the action.

items.en: He boils water himself.
items.wrongPy: qīn zì tā shāo shuǐ
items.why: Put the subject before 亲自, not after it.

items.en: She cooks the food herself.
items.wrongPy: qīn zì tā shāo cài
items.why: The correct order puts 她 before 亲自 and the action after it.

items.note: Put 下来 after a state verb or adjective to describe settling into a state, often becoming quieter, slower, or more stable. Learners sometimes reverse the verb and complement; the state change must come before 下来.

items.en: Grow quiet.
items.wrongPy: xià lai jìng
items.why: The adjective 静 must come before 下来, not after it.

items.en: His fever has gone down.
items.wrongPy: tā de shāo xià lai tuì le
items.why: The state verb 退 must precede 下来, so keep 退下来 together in that order.

items.note: 居然 comes before the predicate to mark a result as surprising or contrary to expectation. It can precede a verb or a phrase such as 在恋爱. Learners sometimes place it after the predicate; keep it before what it modifies.

items.en: He actually got promoted.
items.wrongPy: tā shēng jū rán le
items.why: 居然 must precede the predicate; the correct order is 他居然升了。

items.en: The lock unexpectedly shattered.
items.wrongPy: suǒ suì jū rán le
items.why: 居然 must precede the predicate; the correct order is 锁居然碎了。

items.en: Business has unexpectedly improved.
items.wrongPy: mǎi mai hǎo zhuǎn jū rán le
items.why: 居然 must precede the predicate; the correct order is 买卖居然好转了。

items.en: The secret surprisingly spread.
items.wrongPy: mì mì liú chuán jū rán le
items.why: 居然 must precede the predicate; the correct order is 秘密居然流传了。

items.note: 本 comes before a noun to identify the relevant shop, department, station, or other institution as this or current. Use it when the context makes that institution clear. Learners may wrongly put 本 after the noun; it must directly precede it.

items.en: This shop has security guards.
items.wrongPy: diàn yǒu bǎo ān běn
items.why: 本 must precede 店; the correct phrase is 本店有保安。

items.en: There are new people in this department.
items.wrongPy: chǔ yǒu xīn rén běn
items.why: 本 must precede 处; the correct phrase is 本处有新人。

items.en: This station is about to be upgraded.
items.wrongPy: shēng jí běn tái jí jiāng
items.why: 本台 must stay together as the subject; the correct phrase is 本台即将升级。

items.note: Use 匹 to count horses or bolts of cloth, and 架 for framed machines or aircraft. Put the number and classifier before the noun. Learners often choose a classifier by general shape instead of checking which nouns it counts.

items.en: She picks out two bolts of cloth.
items.wrongPy: tā tiāo liǎng jià bù
items.why: Use 匹 to count bolts of cloth, not 架.

items.en: The lady is choosing a bolt of cloth.
items.wrongPy: tài tai zài tiāo yí jià bù
items.why: Use 匹, the classifier for cloth bolts, instead of 架.

items.note: 替 + a person + a verb phrase means doing something in that person's place or on their behalf. Learners often put the person after the action, but the beneficiary or represented person belongs directly after 替.

items.en: I covered it for him.
items.wrongPy: wǒ tā tì tiē le
items.why: The person must follow 替; say 我替他贴了.

items.en: I fill in the blanks for her.
items.wrongPy: wǒ tā tì tián kōng
items.why: The person must follow 替; say 我替她填空.

items.note: 得 links a verb or adjective to a phrase describing its manner, resulting state, or extent. Use it after the action being described, as in 弯得很深. Learners often put 很 before 得; here, 得 must immediately follow the verb or adjective.

items.en: It fits on very tightly.
items.wrongPy: tào hěn de jǐn
items.why: 得 must immediately follow 套, as in the original order 套得很紧。

items.en: He bends down very far.
items.wrongPy: tā wān hěn de shēn
items.why: 得 must follow 弯 directly, as in 他弯得很深。

items.en: He applies the model skillfully.
items.wrongPy: tā tào hěn de shú liàn
items.why: 得 must follow 套 directly, as in 他套得很熟练。

items.en: He understands it deeply.
items.wrongPy: tā tǐ huì hěn de shēn
items.why: 得 must follow 体会 directly, as in 他体会得很深。

items.note: 头 is a noun-forming suffix in established words such as 念头; it is not the independent noun for “head” in this pattern. Keep the established word order. Learners may mistakenly reverse the two parts of 念头.

items.en: He has an idea.
items.wrongPy: tā yǒu gè tóu niàn
items.why: 念头 is the established word; reversing its parts to 头念 is wrong.

items.en: I have this thought too.
items.wrongPy: wǒ yě yǒu zhè ge tóu niàn
items.why: 念头 is the established word; reversing its parts to 头念 is wrong.

items.note: 万一 introduces an unlikely or unwanted condition, and 就 introduces its consequence. Use the order 万一 + condition, then 就 + consequence; 就 can sometimes be omitted. Learners may move 就 to the end, leaving the consequence clause incomplete.

items.en: If by any chance there is a mistake, quit.
items.wrongPy: wàn yī yǒu shī wù tuì chū jiù
items.why: 就 must come before the consequence 退出, not after it, as in the original order.

items.phrase: 万一有损失我们就退出
items.zh: 万一有损失，我们就退出。
items.en: If there is any loss, we’ll withdraw.
items.wrong: 万一有损失，我们退出就。
items.wrongPy: wàn yī yǒu sǔn shī wǒ men tuì chū jiù
items.why: 就 must come before the consequence 退出, not after it, as in the original order.

items.phrase: 万一他退出我们就退出
items.zh: 万一他退出，我们就退出。
items.en: If he quits, we’ll quit too.
items.wrong: 万一他退出，我们退出就。
items.wrongPy: wàn yī tā tuì chū wǒ men tuì chū jiù
items.why: 就 must come before the consequence 退出, not after it, as in the original order.

items.note: 相当 is a degree adverb placed before a gradable predicate to express a considerable degree. Use it to say something is quite a certain way, not to equate two things. Learners may mistakenly place it after the predicate, as if it were a verb.

items.en: The property management is quite modern.
items.wrongPy: wù yè xiàn dài xiāng dāng
items.why: 相当 must come before 现代, not after the predicate.

items.note: 沿 or 沿着 introduces the route or edge, which comes before the verb phrase. Learners may move the route before 沿, but then the path marker no longer introduces a path and the sentence becomes incorrectly ordered.

items.en: Retreat along the route.
items.wrongPy: lù xiàn yán tuì
items.why: 沿 must introduce the route before the verb; say 沿路线退.

items.en: Act along the route.
items.wrongPy: lù xiàn yán xíng dòng
items.why: 沿 must introduce the route before the verb; say 沿路线行动.

items.note: A look verb can take an object, then a number, then 眼 to count a brief glance. Use this pattern for a quick look at someone or something. Learners may put the number before the object or reverse the order of the number and 眼.

items.en: He gives me a glance.
items.wrongPy: tā tóu wǒ yǎn yī
items.why: The number 一 must come before 眼, not after it.

items.en: She gives him a glance.
items.wrongPy: tā tóu tā yǎn yī
items.why: The counted glance requires 一眼, not 眼一.

items.en: He glanced at me.
items.wrongPy: tā kàn le wǒ yǎn yī
items.why: The number must precede 眼, so 眼一 is the wrong order.

items.note: 同 introduces the person who participates with the subject. Put 同 before that person, then put the verb phrase after the person. Learners sometimes place the person after the verb; that changes the required order and makes the sentence ungrammatical.

items.en: I intern with her.
items.wrongPy: wǒ tóng shí xí tā
items.why: 她 must follow 同 and precede the verb 实习, as in 我同她实习。

items.en: She associates with him.
items.wrongPy: tā tóng jiāo wǎng tā
items.why: 他 must follow 同 and precede the verb 交往, as in 她同他交往。

items.en: I'm willing to strive alongside you.
items.wrongPy: wǒ yuàn tóng zhēng qǔ nǐ
items.why: 你 must follow 同 and precede the verb 争取, as in 我愿同你争取。

items.note: 渐渐 comes before a predicate to describe a development that happens gradually over time. Use it for a change or unfolding state, rather than an abrupt event. Learners may place it after the predicate or put 了 between it and the predicate.

items.en: It gradually straightened.
items.wrongPy: zhí le jiàn jiàn
items.why: 渐渐 must precede the predicate 直了; placing it after the predicate gives the wrong order.

items.note: 再 plus an adjective introduces an extreme or hypothetical degree, followed by 也 and the outcome that remains unchanged. Use it to mean “no matter how.” Learners may omit 也 or put 不 after the verb instead of before it.
可 before an adjective adds colloquial emphasis, and final 了 makes the strong degree sound vivid or newly salient; it does not mark past time here. Learners often put 可 or 了 after the adjective.

items.en: This group is really neat.
items.wrongPy: zhè zǔ kě le zhěng qí
items.why: Final 了 follows the adjective; the correct order is 这组可整齐了.

items.note: 届 is a measure word for a cohort or recurring session, placed after a number and before the event or group name. Use 第 before it for an ordinal. Learners may wrongly place 都 immediately after 届; 都 quantifies the cohort members, not 届.

items.en: The whole cohort of newcomers has arrived.
items.wrongPy: yí jiè dōu xīn rén lái le
items.why: 都 cannot split the cohort noun phrase from its members; place it after 新人, as in the original.

items.en: The new cohort is all very conscientious.
items.wrongPy: yí jiè xīn rén hěn dōu zì jué
items.why: 都 precedes the predicate, while 很 immediately precedes the adjective; the original places them in the required order.

items.note: 尽快 comes before a verb phrase and means doing it as soon as practicable, not necessarily instantly. Learners may place it between a verb and its object; it should modify the whole action from the front.

items.en: Consult a Chinese medicine practitioner as soon as possible.
items.wrongPy: zī xún jǐn kuài zhōng yī
items.why: 尽快 modifies the whole verb phrase and must come before 咨询中医, not between the verb and its object.

items.note: 老是 comes before a predicate to describe repeated or persistent behavior, often with irritation. It does not mean that an action is happening at this exact moment. Learners may mistakenly put it after the verb or at the end of the sentence.

items.en: He is always pursuing freedom.
items.wrongPy: tā zhuī qiú zì yóu lǎo shì
items.why: 老是 must come before the predicate 追求自由, not after the whole action.

items.en: He is always consulting a traditional Chinese medicine doctor.
items.wrongPy: tā zī xún zhōng yī lǎo shì
items.why: 老是 must come before the predicate 咨询中医, not after the whole action.

items.note: 连忙 and 急忙 come before a verb phrase to describe a hurried response to circumstances. Learners often put them after the verb or between the verb and its object; place them before the whole action.

items.en: He hurriedly consulted a Chinese medicine practitioner.
items.wrongPy: tā zī xún lián máng zhōng yī
items.why: 连忙 cannot split the verb from its object here; put it before the whole verb phrase, as in 他连忙咨询中医。

items.note: 时刻 is an adverb meaning “at every moment,” placed after the subject and before its predicate. Use it for a sustained state or action. Learners may move it after the predicate or confuse its position with 都, which belongs before the predicate it scopes over.

items.en: He is always cautious.
items.wrongPy: jǐn shèn tā shí kè
items.why: 时刻 must follow the subject and precede the predicate 谨慎.

items.en: I am always cautious.
items.wrongPy: shí kè jǐn shèn wǒ
items.why: Put 我 before 时刻, then place the predicate after 时刻.

items.en: The newlyweds smile at all times.
items.wrongPy: wēi xiào xīn rén shí kè
items.why: The subject 新人 must come before 时刻 and its predicate 微笑.

items.en: He keeps watch at the competition venue at all times.
items.wrongPy: shǒu sài chǎng shí kè tā
items.why: Put 他 first, then 时刻, followed by the predicate.

items.en: His pain is always there.
items.wrongPy: tā de téng tòng zài dōu shí kè
items.why: 都 belongs before 在, while 时刻 comes before the predicate; neither belongs after 在.

items.en: He consciously pursues freedom at all times.
items.wrongPy: zì jué tā shí kè zhuī qiú zì yóu
items.why: The subject 他 must precede 时刻, which comes before the predicate.

items.note: 早晚 comes before a predicate to make a confident prediction that something will happen sooner or later, without specifying when. Learners often place this time adverb after the verb or its object.

items.en: Freedom will be achieved sooner or later.
items.wrongPy: zì yóu shí xiàn zǎo wǎn
items.why: 早晚 should precede the predicate, not follow 实现; the correct order is 自由早晚实现。

items.en: The newcomers will achieve freedom sooner or later.
items.wrongPy: xīn rén shí xiàn zǎo wǎn zì yóu
items.why: 早晚 cannot split 实现 from its object 自由 here; place it before the predicate, as in 新人早晚实现自由。

items.note: 简直 comes before a predicate to emphasize an extreme assessment or near-equivalence, often hyperbolically. Learners may place it after 是 or inside a noun phrase; keep it before the predicate.

items.en: This organization is simply not serious.
items.wrongPy: zhè zǔ zhī bù jiǎn zhí yán sù
items.why: 简直 should precede the negative predicate 不严肃; the correct order is 这组织简直不严肃。

items.note: 尽量 comes before a verb phrase to express the greatest practicable effort within constraints. Learners often put it between a verb and its object; place it before the whole action.

绝对 is an adverb placed before the predicate to express complete confidence or a firm stance. Use it when emphasizing how strongly someone feels or acts. Learners often put it after the verb or object; keep it directly before the predicate.

items.en: I absolutely respect him.
items.wrongPy: wǒ zūn jìng jué duì tā
items.why: 绝对 must precede the predicate; the correct order is 我绝对尊敬他.

items.en: I absolutely respect this organization.
items.wrongPy: wǒ jué duì zhè ge zǔ zhī zūn jìng
items.why: The object cannot split 绝对 from the predicate this way; say 我绝对尊敬这个组织.

items.note: 较 introduces the comparison target and is followed by that target and the adjective. This is a relatively formal way to say one thing is more adjective than another. Learners may place the target after the adjective; keep it between 较 and the adjective.

items.en: This group is neater than that group.
items.wrongPy: zhè zǔ jiào zhěng qí nà zǔ
items.why: The comparison target must follow 较 and precede the adjective; say 这组较那组整齐.

items.en: This organization is more serious than that one.
items.wrongPy: zhè zǔ zhī jiào yán sù nà zǔ zhī
items.why: The target belongs between 较 and 严肃; the correct order is 这组织较那组织严肃.

items.note: 可 comes before a predicate to add emphasis, a reminder, or a warning; it is not the conjunction “but.” In the first phrase it is followed by 了. Learners may place 可 after the predicate; put it before the predicate instead.

items.en: This group is really neat.
items.wrongPy: zhè zǔ zhěng qí kě le
items.why: 可 must come before the predicate, not after it; say 这组可整齐了.

items.en: You mustn’t chase the pig, you hear?
items.wrongPy: nǐ bù zhǔn kě zhuī zhū
items.why: 可 must precede the predicate 不准追猪; say 你可不准追猪.

items.note: This paired pattern repeats 没 before each of two things that are absent, often to give a negative evaluation. Put each 没 directly before its noun. Learners may move the second 没 to the end; it belongs before the second noun.

items.en: Without resources, without freedom.
items.wrongPy: méi zī yuán zì yóu méi
items.why: The second 没 must precede 自由, not appear at the end; the correct phrase is 没资源没自由.

items.note: This pattern says that once someone says they will do an action, they do that same action immediately. Repeat the action around 就; learners often put 就 after the second action.

items.en: He says he’ll withdraw, and then he does.
items.wrongPy: tā shuō tuì tuì jiù
items.why: 就 is misplaced after both 退 actions; it should come between them.

items.en: As soon as they say they’ll change, they change.
items.wrongPy: shuō zhuǎn biàn zhuǎn biàn jiù
items.why: 就 is misplaced after both 转变 actions; it should come between them.

items.note: This paired pattern presents different people doing different actions: one group does the first verb and another the second. Keep 的 after each verb; learners often omit or duplicate it.

items.en: Some grab, and others chase.
items.wrongPy: zhuā de de zhuā zhuī de zhuī
items.why: 的 is duplicated after 抓; use one 的 to mark the repeated action pair.

items.en: Some of them argue, while others withdraw.
items.wrongPy: tā men zhēng de de zhēng tuì de tuì
items.why: 的 is duplicated after 争; use one 的 to mark the repeated action pair.

items.note: Use verb 着 verb 着 to show an action continuing until another event happens. 着 marks the ongoing process; learners often repeat the verb but omit 着 or add an extra one.

items.en: While chasing, someone bumped into something.
items.wrongPy: zhuī zhe zhe zhuī zhe zhuàng le
items.why: 着 is duplicated after the first 追; only one 着 belongs between the repeated verbs.

items.note: 依据 introduces the grounds or standard, which comes before the action phrase. Use it for actions guided by needs, reality, or another basis; learners may put the basis after the action or mistake it for the action's object.

items.en: Change the style according to the needs.
items.wrongPy: yī jù xū qiú bù zhuǎn biàn yàng shì
items.why: 不 negates the action, changing the affirmative instruction to not changing the style.

items.en: Change the style according to reality.
items.wrongPy: yī jù xiàn shí bù zhuǎn biàn yàng shì
items.why: 不 negates the action, changing the affirmative instruction to not changing the style.

items.phrase: 依据总体需求组织资源
items.zh: 依据总体需求组织资源
items.en: Organize resources according to overall needs.
items.wrong: 依据总体需求不组织资源
items.wrongPy: yī jù zǒng tǐ xū qiú bù zǔ zhī zī yuán
items.why: 不 negates the action, changing the affirmative instruction to not organizing resources.

items.note: Use this paired pattern when two proposed actions both feel unacceptable, expressing a dilemma rather than simply classifying them. Learners often leave out the second 也 or mistake the construction for a neutral either-or statement.

items.en: Chasing isn’t right, and retreating isn’t right either.
items.wrongPy: zhuī bú shì yě tuì yě bú shì
items.why: 也 is misplaced after 不是; the correct clause is 追也不是.

items.en: Chasing isn’t right, but quitting isn’t right either.
items.wrongPy: zhuī yě bú shì tuì chū bú shì yě
items.why: 也 is misplaced after 不是; the correct clause is 退出也不是.

items.phrase: 追求也不是退出也不是
items.zh: 追求也不是，退出也不是
items.en: Pursuing it feels wrong, but quitting feels wrong too.
items.wrong: 追求不是也，退出也不是
items.wrongPy: zhuī qiú bú shì yě tuì chū yě bú shì
items.why: 也 is misplaced after 不是; the correct clause is 追求也不是.

items.note: Use this pattern to say that one person or thing fills both contrasting roles or produces both outcomes. Keep 是它 in each clause, with 也 before the second 是; learners often move 也 to the end.

items.en: He’s the owner, and he’s also the host.
items.wrongPy: zhǔ rén shì tā zhǔ chí yě tā shì
items.why: 也 must come before 是他; the correct second clause is 主持也是他.

items.note: Use this pattern for an ongoing or idle state when suggesting that one might as well do something else. Learners often separate 着 from its verb; it must follow the verb in both clauses.

items.en: Since I’m idle anyway…
items.wrongPy: xián yě shì zhe xián zhe
items.why: 着 must attach directly to 闲; the correct order is 闲着也是闲着.

items.en: I'm standing guard anyway.
items.wrongPy: shǒu yě shì zhe shǒu zhe
items.why: 着 must attach directly to 守; the correct order is 守着也是守着.

items.note: This paired pattern says neither of two actions is permissible or workable. Repeat each action around 也; learners often omit 也 or mix the verbs across the pair.

items.phrase: 追也追不得退也退不得
items.zh: 追也追不得，退也退不得
items.en: You can neither chase nor retreat.
items.wrongPy: zhuī zhuī bù dé tuì yě tuì bù dé
items.why: The first action needs 也 before its repeated verb; without it, the fixed paired pattern is broken.

items.phrase: 争也争不得退也退不得
items.zh: 争也争不得，退也退不得
items.en: I can neither fight for it nor back out.
items.wrongPy: zhēng yě zhēng bù dé tuì tuì bù dé
items.why: The second action needs 也 before its repeated verb; without it, the fixed paired pattern is broken.

items.phrase: 撞也撞不得抓也抓不得
items.zh: 撞也撞不得，抓也抓不得
items.en: You can't bump into it or grab it.
items.wrongPy: zhuàng zhuàng bù dé zhuā yě zhuā bù dé
items.why: The first action needs 也 before its repeated verb; without it, the fixed paired pattern is broken.

items.note: 不管怎样说 introduces a conclusion that holds despite different accounts or evaluations. Put 都 before the predicate in the following clause; learners often place 都 after the subject or 很.
不 + verb + 白不 + the same verb expresses that refusing an available benefit would gain nothing. Keep 白不 together before the repeated verb; learners often omit the second 不.

items.en: If picking it is free, you might as well pick it.
items.wrongPy: bù zhāi bái zhāi
items.why: The second 摘 must be negated in 白不摘; otherwise the expression loses its required negative form.

items.en: If there’s a discount, you might as well use it.
items.wrongPy: yǒu yōu huì bái bú yòng yòng
items.why: 白 must follow 不用, forming 不用白不用; moving it to the front breaks the construction.

items.note: Use the same verb on both sides of 什么 to reject or reproach an action, often with an exclamatory tone. Learners may omit the echoed verb or put 什么 after it; the frame is verb + 什么 + the same verb.

items.en: Stop arguing!
items.wrongPy: shén me zhēng zhēng
items.why: 什么 must follow the first verb; the correct order is 争什么争！

items.en: Stop chasing!
items.wrongPy: zhuī shén me zhuī zhuī
items.why: This repeats the verb an extra time; the echoed pattern has just one 追 on each side of 什么.

items.note: 真有 + person + 的 expresses impressed surprise and can also sound sarcastic depending on context. Keep 的 after the person. Learners may wrongly place 的 before the person, breaking this fixed pattern.

items.en: Nice one!
items.wrongPy: zhēn yǒu de nǐ
items.why: 的 must follow 你 in this expression; the correct order is 真有你的！

items.en: She’s really something!
items.wrongPy: zhēn yǒu de tā
items.why: 的 must follow 她 in this expression; the correct order is 真有她的！

items.en: He's really something!
items.wrongPy: zhēn yǒu de tā
items.why: 的 must follow 他 in this expression; the correct order is 真有他的！

items.note: Compatible adverbials can appear together before the verb phrase, with their order depending on meaning and scope. Learners should not assume any order is possible: 都 and 很, for example, cannot be freely swapped in 他一辈子都很有学问.
Repeat a verb with 来 and 去 to describe repeated attempts or back-and-forth action, then state the conclusion with 都是 or 就是. Learners may leave out 来 or 去, but the repeated frame needs both.

items.en: Bumping around, it always ends in an accident.
items.wrongPy: zhuàng lái zhuàng dōu shì yì wài
items.why: The repeated-action frame needs 去 after the second 撞; the correct phrase is 撞来撞去。

items.phrase: 追来追去都是追求自由
items.zh: 追来追去，都是追求自由。
items.en: Chasing back and forth, it all comes down to pursuing freedom.
items.wrongPy: zhuī lái zhuī dōu shì zhuī qiú zì yóu
items.why: The repeated-action frame needs 去 after the second 追; the correct phrase is 追来追去。

items.phrase: 争来争去都是争取自由
items.zh: 争来争去，都是争取自由。
items.en: They argue back and forth; it’s all about seeking freedom.
items.wrongPy: zhēng lái zhēng dōu shì zhēng qǔ zì yóu
items.why: The repeated-action frame needs 去 after the second 争; the correct phrase is 争来争去。

items.note: Use this pattern to signal that you accept whatever someone says or decides as final; learners often wrongly omit the repeated 什么 or treat 就 as mandatory, though it may drop.
Place 得 before a compatible fixed expression to describe the resulting state or degree, as in 得很整齐. Learners may drop 得 or move 很 to the end, but these change the required complement structure.

items.en: This group is very orderly.
items.wrongPy: zhè zǔ zhěng qí hěn
items.why: The fixed degree expression is 整齐得很; omitting 得 makes this sequence ungrammatical.

items.en: This combination is arranged very neatly.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge zǔ hé de zhěng qí hěn
items.why: 很 belongs before 整齐 in this complement; the correct phrase is 这个组合得很整齐。

items.note: Attach 下去 after a state or adjective to say that it continues into the future, rather than describing downward movement. A common mistake is placing 下去 before the state; it follows the state it modifies.

items.en: He will continue to suffer.
items.wrongPy: tā huì xià qù tòng kǔ
items.why: 下去 follows 痛苦 to mark continuation; the correct order is 他会痛苦下去.

items.note: This emphatic frame dismisses a topic by echoing a predicate with 不 between its two occurrences; final 的 can be omitted. Learners often move 不 or treat the two halves as separate questions.

items.en: What’s all this talk about organizations!
items.wrongPy: shén me bù zǔ zhī zǔ zhī de
items.why: 不 belongs between the repeated predicate, not before it; the required frame is 组织不组织.

items.en: What do you mean, free or not free!
items.wrongPy: shén me bú zì yóu zì yóu de
items.why: 不 belongs between the repeated predicate, not before it; the required frame is 自由不自由.

items.en: Urgent or not, what does it matter!
items.wrongPy: shén me jí qiè jí qiè bù de
items.why: 不 belongs between the repeated predicate, not after both copies; the required frame is 急切不急切.

items.note: Put 得 or 不得 after a compatible verb to say an action is practicable or permissible, or forbidden. Learners often put 不得 before the verb; this pattern places it after the verb.

items.en: This pig must not be chased.
items.wrongPy: zhè zhū zhuī de bù dé
items.why: The extra 得 makes the ending ungrammatical; the negative permission form is 这猪追不得.

items.en: This pig must not be caught.
items.wrongPy: zhè zhū zhuā de bù dé
items.why: The extra 得 makes the ending ungrammatical; the negative permission form is 这猪抓不得.

items.note: Place 把 before a known object, then put 一 immediately before the verb for a brisk single action, often with an immediate consequence. A common mistake is moving 一 before the object instead of keeping it before the verb.

items.en: He grabs the pig in one quick motion.
items.wrongPy: tā bǎ yì zhuā zhū
items.why: 一 belongs after the object and before the verb; the correct order is 他把猪一抓.

items.en: He quickly adjusts the volume.
items.wrongPy: tā bǎ yì tiáo yīn liàng
items.why: 一 belongs after the object and before the verb; the correct order is 他把音量一调.

items.note: With compatible verbs such as 怀, 印, 贴, and 摆, 有 follows the verb and introduces what is held, printed, posted, or displayed. Learners may put 有 before the verb; that changes the construction and is wrong here.

This pattern links two actions by the same subject, with the first causing or leading to the second; it is useful for compact narratives. Learners may reverse the actions, making the cause follow its result.

This compact pattern says that without the first condition or action, the consequence does not happen. It is useful for stating dependencies. Learners may put 不 in the wrong place instead of placing it before the condition or consequence.

items.en: Without seeking freedom, you cannot gain freedom.
items.wrongPy: bú zì yóu zhuī qiú bù dé zì yóu
items.why: 自由 is misplaced before 追求; the correct sentence is 不追求自由，不得自由。

items.note: Use 可见 after evidence to introduce the conclusion inferred from it. Keep the proposition after 可见; learners may incorrectly put the proposition’s subject after its predicate.

items.en: He is quarreling; evidently, he feels uneasy.
items.wrongPy: tā chǎo jià kě jiàn bù ān tā
items.why: 不安 must precede its subject 他; the correct conclusion is 他不安.

items.en: He made a mistake, so clearly he isn’t skilled.
items.wrongPy: tā shī wù kě jiàn bù shú liàn tā
items.why: The subject 他 must precede 不熟练; the correct conclusion is 他不熟练.

items.note: This paired pattern says that without the first noun phrase, the second is absent: 没有 X，就没有 Y. Learners may put 没有 after the second noun phrase; keep it directly before each noun phrase.

items.en: Without resources, there is no freedom.
items.wrongPy: méi yǒu zī yuán jiù zì yóu méi yǒu
items.why: 没有 must come before 自由; the correct phrase is 就没有自由.

items.note: This pattern states a measured gap between two things, using a relational adjective followed by a comparison target and a difference. It is not a general substitute for 比; learners wrongly apply it to any adjective. The supplied phrase is only an ordinary adjective sentence.

Put the condition action before the dependent action: doing the first makes the second possible or produces its result. Learners may misplace particles or adverbs, or reverse the actions; preserve the stated action sequence.
Put 得不得了 after a mental verb or adjective to express an exceptionally intense state or degree. Learners may place 不得了 before the description, but the 得不得了 complement must follow it.

items.en: He is terribly distressed.
items.wrongPy: tā bù dé liǎo tòng kǔ
items.why: 不得了 must follow the description with 得; the correct order is 他痛苦得不得了。

items.en: She is incredibly innocent.
items.wrongPy: tā bù dé liǎo tiān zhēn
items.why: 不得了 must follow the description with 得; the correct order is 她天真得不得了。

items.en: He is extremely serious.
items.wrongPy: tā bù dé liǎo yán sù
items.why: 不得了 must follow the description with 得; the correct order is 他严肃得不得了。

items.note: Use 为的是 after an action to foreground the purpose intended by that action. It introduces the goal, not another action in a sequence. Learners often omit 的, but the pattern here is 为的是, not 为是.

items.en: Studying is for advancing to the next stage of school.
items.wrongPy: niàn shū wèi shì shēng xué
items.why: 为的是 requires 的; the correct version is 念书为的是升学。

items.phrase: 他们交谈为的是消除误解
items.zh: 他们交谈，为的是消除误解
items.en: They converse in order to clear up the misunderstanding.
items.wrong: 他们交谈，为是消除误解
items.wrongPy: tā men jiāo tán wèi shì xiāo chú wù jiě
items.why: 为的是 requires 的 before the purpose; the correct version is 他们交谈，为的是消除误解。

items.phrase: 他注重语音为的是主持直播
items.zh: 他注重语音，为的是主持直播。
items.en: He focuses on pronunciation in order to host a livestream.
items.wrong: 他注重语音，为是主持直播。
items.wrongPy: tā zhù zhòng yǔ yīn wèi shì zhǔ chí zhí bō
items.why: The purpose marker is 为的是, so the correct version is 他注重语音，为的是主持直播。

items.note: Place 白 immediately before the verb phrase to say the action produced no intended benefit. It modifies the action, not its result; learners may move it after the verb or mistake it for a description of color.

items.en: He promoted it in vain.
items.wrongPy: tā bái le xuān chuán
items.why: 了 cannot come between 白 and its verb; the correct phrase is 他白宣传了。

items.phrase: 她白白下功夫厂家不录用她
items.zh: 她白白下功夫，厂家不录用她。
items.en: She worked hard for nothing; the company didn’t hire her.
items.wrong: 她白白功夫下，厂家不录用她。
items.wrongPy: tā bái bái gōng fu xià chǎng jiā bú lù yòng tā
items.why: 白白 must precede the verb phrase 下功夫; the correct phrase is 她白白下功夫，厂家不录用她。

items.note: Use 由 + components + 组成 to state what makes up a whole; name the whole first, then its components. Learners often omit 由 or put 组成 before the component phrase.

items.phrase: 这个体系由多媒体组成
items.zh: 这个体系由多媒体组成。
items.en: This system is made up of multimedia.
items.wrong: 这个体系组成由多媒体。
items.wrongPy: zhè ge tǐ xì zǔ chéng yóu duō méi tǐ
items.why: 由 must introduce the components before 组成; the correct order is 这个体系由多媒体组成。

items.note: This pattern places two contrasting actions or facts side by side, often with the same subject; context clarifies the contrast. Learners may put 也 in the wrong position: it normally precedes the verb it modifies.

items.en: Towns have high-rises and farmland too.
items.wrong: 城镇有也高层，也有农田。
items.wrongPy: chéng zhèn yǒu yě gāo céng yě yǒu nóng tián
items.why: 也 cannot be placed between 有 and its object here; the correct sentence is 城镇有高层，也有农田。

items.phrase: 他注重休闲不注重业务
items.zh: 他注重休闲，不注重业务。
items.en: He values leisure, not business.
items.wrong: 他注重休闲，不业务注重。
items.wrongPy: tā zhù zhòng xiū xián bú yè wù zhù zhòng
items.why: The second clause puts the object before its verb; the correct sentence is 他注重休闲，不注重业务。

items.phrase: 他尊敬主人不尊敬组织
items.zh: 他尊敬主人，不尊敬组织
items.en: He respects the host but not the organization.
items.wrong: 他尊敬主人，不组织尊敬。
items.wrongPy: tā zūn jìng zhǔ rén bù zǔ zhī zūn jìng
items.why: The second clause puts the object before its verb; the correct sentence is 他尊敬主人，不尊敬组织。

items.note: 较 goes before an adjective to express a relative degree against an unstated baseline, especially in written Chinese. It modifies the adjective, not the noun or subject. Learners often put 较 after the adjective or between a subject and noun.

items.en: The positioning is relatively clear.
items.wrongPy: qīng xī jiào dìng wèi
items.why: 较 must precede the adjective it modifies; the correct order is 较清晰.

items.en: This organization is relatively serious.
items.wrongPy: zhè jiào zǔ zhī yán sù
items.why: 较 belongs before the adjective, not between 这 and 组织; put it before 严肃.

items.en: Our organization is relatively free.
items.wrongPy: wǒ men de jiào zǔ zhī zì yóu
items.why: 较 must precede the adjective 自由, not come between the possessive phrase and its noun.

items.note: Attach 起来 after a state verb or adjective to show that a state emerges or develops. Learners may put 起来 before the state word, but it follows the state it marks as developing.

items.en: He became serious.
items.wrongPy: tā qǐ lai yán sù
items.why: 起来 follows the state word; the correct order is 他严肃起来。

items.en: They united.
items.wrongPy: tā men qǐ lai tuán jié le
items.why: 起来 follows 团结; the correct order is 他们团结起来了。

items.en: The drinking water is getting warm.
items.wrongPy: yǐn yòng shuǐ le nuǎn qǐ lai
items.why: 了 belongs after 起来 here; the correct order is 饮用水暖起来了。

items.en: The comments started to crowd together.
items.wrongPy: píng lùn dōu qǐ lai mì jí
items.why: 起来 follows 密集; the correct order is 评论都密集起来。

items.en: The atmosphere became lively.
items.wrongPy: fēn wéi qǐ lai huó yuè le
items.why: 起来 follows 活跃; the correct order is 氛围活跃起来了。

items.note: 有着 comes before a noun phrase to describe sustained possession or existence, especially in descriptive or written Chinese. Learners may move 着 away from 有; it belongs directly after 有 in this pattern.

items.en: The organization has its own needs.
items.wrongPy: zǔ zhī yǒu zì shēn zhe xū qiú
items.why: 着 must follow 有 rather than 自身; the correct sentence is 组织有着自身需求。

items.en: He has a firm belief.
items.wrongPy: tā jiān dìng de yǒu zhe xìn niàn
items.why: The modifier is misplaced before the verb; the correct sentence is 他有着坚定的信念。
